E4021: Payment authorization expired
Cause: The authorization hold lapsed before capture.
Handling: Re-authorize, then capture. Do not retry capture alone.
Retryable: False

## Service map
The platform is eight services behind one gateway. The gateway terminates TLS,
applies rate limits, and forwards to users, auth, orders, payments,
notifications, reporting, and search. Services call each other over internal
HTTP with the caller's session token forwarded only to the users and auth
services; every other internal call uses the calling service's own credential.
Orders calls payments to authorize and capture, payments calls notifications
when a capture succeeds or fails, and reporting reads a replica of the orders
and payments databases rather than calling either service.

## Order lifecycle
An order starts as a quote. Adding a payment authorization moves it to pending.
Capture moves it to paid. Only paid orders appear in revenue reports, which is why
the paid-total report filters on status rather than on the presence of a payment row.
A cancelled order keeps its rows; cancellation releases any inventory reservation
and voids an uncaptured authorization.

## Authorization and capture
Payments authorizes when the order moves to pending and captures later, from the
capture worker, CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES after authorization. The delay exists so that
an order edited within a few minutes of checkout can be re-authorized without a
refund. The provider holds an authorization for AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES; a hold that
lapses before the worker captures produces E4021 on capture. Capture is idempotent
by order id, so a second capture of the same order returns E5011 and is treated as
success. Captures that fail with a retryable provider error are retried up to
MAX_CAPTURE_RETRIES times with exponential backoff.

PAYMENT_BASE_URL       string    True      None                 Provider endpoint. Sandbox and live endpoints differ.
PROVIDER_REGION        string    False     us                   Provider region; must match the merchant account.
CAPTURE_TIMEOUT        integer   False     30                   Seconds to wait for a capture call before failing it.
CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES  integer   False     15                   Minutes after authorization that the capture worker captures.
AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES      integer   False     60                   Minutes the provider holds an authorization. Must exceed CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES or holds lapse before capture.
WEBHOOK_SECRET         string    True      (value not shown)    Shared secret for verifying provider webhooks.
MAX_CAPTURE_RETRIES    integer   False     4                    Capture retries on retryable provider errors.

part.text:
**E4021 means “Payment authorization expired.”** The provider’s authorization hold expired before the payments capture worker attempted capture.

The likely misconfiguration is in `config/staging/payments.conf`:

| Setting | Current value | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES` (line 5) | `15` | Worker captures 15 minutes after authorization. |
| `AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES` (line 6) | `10` | Authorization expires after 10 minutes. |

The configuration schema explicitly requires **`AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES > CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES`**. Staging currently schedules capture five minutes after the authorization expires, which explains E4021.

**Recommended change:** Increase `AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES` to a provider-supported duration greater than 15 minutes—for example, the schema default of `60`, if supported by the staging provider. Alternatively, reduce the capture delay below 10 minutes, leaving sufficient margin for worker scheduling. Ensure the configured hold duration matches the provider’s actual behavior.

For payments already affected, **re-authorize, then capture**. E4021 is not retryable; retrying capture alone will not resolve it.

The other visible settings have no obvious schema violations. `PAYMENT_API_KEY` and `WEBHOOK_SECRET` are supplied by the secrets manager, so their values were not verified. No files were edited.
